title: Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture
formal: Does every finite clutter with the packing property have the max-flow min-cut property? Equivalently, if every deletion/contraction minor satisfies unweighted integral packing–covering equality, must weighted integral packing–covering equality hold for every nonnegative integer weight vector?
definitions:
A clutter \(\mathcal C\) on a finite ground set \(E\) is a family of subsets of \(E\), no one properly containing another. Its original members are nonempty; the empty family is allowed. A cover is a set \(T\subseteq E\) meeting every member, and \(	au(\mathcal C)\) is its minimum cardinality. A packing is a family of pairwise disjoint members; \(
u(\mathcal C)\) is its maximum cardinality. Deleting an element removes it from the ground set and discards all members containing it. Contracting an element removes it from the ground set and from every member, then keeps only inclusion-minimal members. A minor is obtained by any finite sequence of these operations, including the empty sequence. The packing property is \(	au(\mathcal D)=
u(\mathcal D)\) for every minor \(\mathcal D\). For the empty family both numbers are zero. For the degenerate minor \(\{\varnothing\}\), set both numbers to \(+\infty\): no cover exists and arbitrarily many copies of the empty member can be packed. These conventions give no obstruction from degenerate minors. For an original clutter and capacities \(w\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{E}\), define \[	au_w(\mathcal C)=\min\left\{\sum_{e\in T}w_e:T\subseteq E	ext{ is a cover}ight\},\qquad 
u_w(\mathcal C)=\max\left\{\sum_{F\in\mathcal C}y_F:y\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{\mathcal C},\ \sum_{F
i e}y_F\le w_e	ext{ for every }e\in Eight\}.\] Multiplicities \(y_F\) allow repeated packed members, and every copy consumes one unit of capacity at each of its elements. Both optima are finite because original members are nonempty. The max-flow min-cut (MFMC) property is equality of these optima for every nonnegative integer capacity vector; the weights and ground-set size have no fixed upper bound.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the universal implication, or of its logical negation. An affirmative answer must establish \(\tau_w(\mathcal C)=\nu_w(\mathcal C)\) for every clutter with the packing property and every nonnegative integer vector \(w\). A negative answer must exhibit a finite clutter and such a vector with \(\tau_w(\mathcal C)>\nu_w(\mathcal C)\), and verify the packing property for every minor. A finite census, a proper subclass theorem, or fractional duality alone is insufficient.

context_blocks.text: Packing and covering often give two descriptions of the same combinatorial optimum. In a clutter, the unweighted equality can fail. Requiring equality after every deletion and contraction removes many such obstructions. The Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture asks whether this local robustness already guarantees equality for every integer capacity vector.

For a concrete example, take E as the vertices of a bipartite graph and the clutter members as its edges. Covers are vertex covers and packings are matchings. This illustrates the familiar kind of min–max equality that the general conjecture seeks to characterize, without restricting its input to graph edge families.

For the member-by-element incidence matrix \(A\), whose entry \(A_{F,e}\) is one precisely when \(e\in F\), the corresponding fractional problems are \(\min\{w^{\mathsf T}z:Az\ge\mathbf1,\ z\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le w,\ y\ge0\}\). The conjectured equality concerns integer solutions, and hence is stronger than ordinary linear-programming duality. It asks for integral optima on both sides for every integer weight.

Schrijver’s Survey Question 68 calls the target the assertion that every packing hypergraph is Mengerian. The terminology differs, but its packing property includes all minors and its conclusion includes arbitrary nonnegative integer weights. Checking only the all-ones weight on the original instance would yield a much weaker, insufficient hypothesis.

Abdi and Schwarcz’s July 2026 manuscript calls the statement the replication conjecture and explicitly retains it as open. It reports verification for clutters on at most ten elements and for a specified bounded-degree family of cuboids. These are finite or restricted confirmations, not a proof for arbitrary ground-set size.

The same work gives a finite set of weight vectors sufficient to test the MFMC property of a fixed clutter, with an improved bound on their entries. This makes checking individual instances more effective. The number and size of possible clutters still grow without bound, so instance-wise testability does not prove the universal implication.

Roy and Saha report a proof for \((n-2)\)-uniform clutters: every member has size exactly \(n-2\) when the ground set has \(n\) elements. Arbitrary clutters can have unrelated member sizes, so this subclass result leaves the stated universal implication unchanged.

why: Identify whether all obstructions to weighted integral packing–covering duality are already visible as unweighted failures in minors, a central issue in integer programming and combinatorial optimization.

importance.reason: A central conjecture connecting minor obstructions, integral linear programming and packing–covering duality. Schrijver treats it as a major survey question, and a July 2026 primary paper develops both theoretical and computational methods around it.

progress.text: Schrijver lists the packing-to-Mengerian implication as Survey Question 68.
Roy–Saha v2 reports the conjecture for \((n-2)\)-uniform clutters, with \(n\) the ground-set size. This is a restricted family.
Abdi–Schwarcz v2 reports finite verification through ten ground-set elements and an improved finite-weight test, while leaving the universal conjecture open.

sentences: A clutter is a finite family of sets with no redundant containing member.
Its packing property requires unweighted packing–covering equality in every deletion and contraction minor.
The conjecture asks whether this already implies equality for every nonnegative integer capacity vector.
Weighted packings may repeat members within those capacities.
Recent source results cover finite ground-set sizes and restricted families, while retaining the general question.
